name: Animal
summary: Materials that come from animals: meat, fish, milk, eggs, hide and leather, hair and silk fibres, shell, horn and feather.

materials.name: Alpaca and vicuña
materials.summary: Andean weavers used alpaca and vicuña fibre in the Paracas textiles; vicuña is the finest animal fibre in commercial use.
materials.photo: a loose hank of alpaca and vicuña fibre

materials.name: Cashmere
materials.summary: The down of the Changthangi goat, woven into Kashmir shawls; Europe took the shawl as fashion from about 1800.
materials.photo: a loose hank of cashmere fibre

materials.name: Human hair
materials.summary: Hair of a loved person, woven or set under glass in mourning and sentimental jewels of the 19th century. Mourning rings with hair are known from the 17th century.
materials.photo: a loose hank of human hair fibre

materials.name: Merino wool
materials.summary: Spain bred the fine merino sheep from about the 14th century and banned its export until the 18th century.
materials.photo: a loose hank of merino wool fibre

materials.name: Mohair
materials.summary: The hair of the Angora goat; it gives a lustrous, springy yarn for suiting and knitwear.
materials.photo: a loose hank of mohair fibre

materials.name: Silk
materials.summary: China reeled silk from the cocoon of Bombyx mori; Byzantium got silkworms in about AD 552.
materials.photo: a loose hank of silk fibre

materials.name: Wool
materials.summary: Sheep with a woolly fleece appear in Mesopotamia in the fourth millennium BC; before that, sheep had hair.
materials.photo: a loose hank of wool fibre
materials.photo_applied: a folded wool throw on a chair

materials.name: Bone ash
materials.photo: a small heap of bone ash powder

materials.name: Butter
materials.summary: The fat of the northern French kitchen; it took the place of oil and lard in sauces after 1650.

materials.name: Cheese
materials.summary: Strainers with milk fat from about 5500 BC; Parmigiano, Comté and Gruyère are hard cheeses for cooking.

materials.name: Cream
materials.summary: Double cream and crème fraîche thicken and enrich the sauces of the classic kitchen.

materials.name: Milk
materials.photo: a small glass dish of milk

materials.name: Hen egg
materials.summary: Binds, raises, thickens and emulsifies: the tool of mayonnaise, hollandaise, soufflé and custard.

materials.name: Lard
materials.summary: Rendered pork fat; the frying fat of medieval and peasant kitchens.

materials.name: Feather
materials.summary: Ostrich, egret and other plumes that trimmed the hat; the Victorian trade in plumes and whole birds led to the first bird-protection laws.

materials.name: Goose down
materials.summary: The under-plumage of geese, in quilted baffles; Eddie Bauer patented the quilted down jacket after a near-fatal fishing trip.
materials.photo: a small heap of goose down

materials.name: Felt
materials.summary: A cloth of matted fibres with no weave; the Pazyryk graves held felt saddle cloths and hangings. The cloth of hats.

materials.name: Loden
materials.summary: A fulled and napped wool that sheds rain and wind; the coat cloth of the Alpine countries.

materials.name: Caviar
materials.summary: Salted sturgeon roe; a luxury of the Russian court and the French restaurant.

materials.name: Cod
materials.summary: Dried as stockfish and salted as klippfisk; traded from Lofoten through the Middle Ages.

materials.name: Salmon
materials.summary: Wild in rivers, then farmed after 1970; cured, smoked or cooked pink.

materials.name: Sole and flat fish
materials.summary: Dover sole, turbot and brill: the fish of the classic kitchen, poached, grilled or meunière.

materials.name: Tuna
materials.summary: Raw as sushi in Japan after the 1840s; the fat belly is toro.

materials.name: Game birds
materials.summary: Pheasant, partridge, woodcock and pigeon; the medieval feast added swan, heron and peacock.

materials.name: Venison
materials.summary: Red deer, roe deer and reindeer; hung, roasted and served with a sharp berry sauce.

materials.name: Hide (raw animal skin)
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of hide

materials.name: Fur
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of fur

materials.name: Horn
materials.summary: Animal horn, heated and pressed or carved; it takes a translucent, amber-like colour and was a main material of Art Nouveau combs and pendants.

materials.name: Whalebone (baleen)
materials.summary: Plates of baleen from whales; thin strips of it stiffened stays and corsets until spring steel and plastic replaced it.

materials.name: Calfskin
materials.summary: Fine, tight-grained leather from calves for dress shoes, gloves and small leather goods.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of calfskin

materials.name: Chrome-tanned leather
materials.summary: Hide tanned with chromium salts in hours, not months; Augustus Schultz made the process commercial in 1884. Most leather now is chrome tanned.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of chrome-tanned leather

materials.name: Exotic skin
materials.summary: Crocodile, alligator, ostrich and lizard skin; trade in most species is under CITES control since 1975.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of exotic skin

materials.name: Kidskin
materials.summary: Soft, thin goatskin for gloves, evening shoes and linings.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of kidskin

materials.name: Leather
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of leather

materials.name: Patent leather
materials.summary: Leather with a hard, high-gloss lacquer; the shoe of evening dress and the 1960s boot.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of patent leather

materials.name: Shagreen
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of shagreen

materials.name: Shearling
materials.summary: Sheepskin with the wool left on; the bomber jacket, the boot and the coat lining.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of shearling

materials.name: Sheepskin
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of sheepskin

materials.name: Shell cordovan
materials.summary: Dense leather from the shell under the hide of a horse's rump; the cordwainers of Córdoba gave the trade its name.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of shell cordovan

materials.name: Suede
materials.summary: Leather with the flesh side napped; the name comes from 'gants de Suède', Swedish gloves.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of suede

materials.name: Vegetable-tanned leather
materials.summary: Hide tanned with bark tannins; a cowhide shoe from the Areni-1 cave is about 5,500 years old. It darkens and takes a patina.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of vegetable-tanned leather

materials.name: Beef
materials.summary: The fillet, the rib and the braising cuts; tournedos Rossini and boeuf bourguignon.

materials.name: Lamb
materials.summary: Saddle, rack and leg; the roast of spring.

materials.name: Pork
materials.summary: Fresh, salted and cured; lard is its fat.

materials.name: Veal
materials.summary: The meat of the calf and the bones of the white and brown stock.

materials.name: Tulle (bobbinet)
materials.summary: A hexagonal net from Heathcoat's bobbinet machine; the cloth of the veil, the petticoat and the tutu.

materials.name: Chicken
materials.summary: The capon and the Bresse chicken of the French kitchen.

materials.name: Duck
materials.summary: Breast cooked pink and legs as confit; Peking duck in China.

materials.name: Foie gras
materials.summary: Fattened goose or duck liver; a mark of the French luxury kitchen since the eighteenth century.

materials.name: Shellac
materials.photo: a small glass dish of shellac

materials.name: Flat-weave rug
materials.photo_applied: a flat-weave wool rug on a floor
materials.photo: a folded swatch of flat-weave rug

materials.name: Hand-woven wool rug
materials.photo_applied: a hand-woven wool rug on a floor
materials.photo: a folded swatch of hand-woven wool rug

materials.name: Conch shell
materials.summary: The pink and white layers of the conch shell, carved as a cameo; popular in Victorian jewellery. Italian carvers cut shell cameos from the 16th century.

materials.name: Cultured pearl
materials.summary: A pearl grown around a nucleus that a person put in the oyster; it made the pearl necklace a jewel of the middle class.

materials.name: Natural pearl
materials.summary: A pearl that grew in an oyster with no help; the most costly jewel of the court era.

materials.name: Tortoiseshell
materials.summary: The shell of the hawksbill turtle for combs, frames and boxes; CITES ended the trade, and acetate copies the pattern.
materials.photo: a square sample sheet of tortoiseshell

materials.name: Oyster
materials.summary: Sergius Orata farmed oysters at Baiae; eaten raw or poached.

materials.name: Sea urchin
materials.summary: Raw gonads, sweet and briny; uni in Japan.

materials.name: Shellfish
materials.summary: Lobster, langoustine, crab, scallop and prawn; the luxury of the coast.

materials.name: Stock (broth)
materials.photo: a small glass dish of stock

materials.name: Honey
materials.summary: The sweetener of Europe before sugar.

materials.name: Aran knit
materials.summary: A thick cream knit of cables, diamonds and moss stitch; it became a fashion knit in the 1950s.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of aran knit

materials.name: Boiled wool
materials.summary: A wool knit that heat, water and rubbing shrink into a dense, felt-like cloth that does not fray; Tyrolean walk jackets were made of it, and Japanese designers of the 1980s used it for sculpted coats.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of boiled wool

materials.name: Cashmere knit
materials.summary: A fine knit of cashmere down, the luxury form of knitwear; the fibre came to Europe in Kashmir shawls, and plain cashmere jumpers became a sign of quiet wealth.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of cashmere knit

materials.name: Fair Isle knit
materials.summary: A stranded knit in two colours each row; the Prince of Wales wore a Fair Isle jumper to golf in 1921.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of fair isle knit

materials.name: Frame-knit hosiery
materials.summary: Stockings from the knitting frame, the first textile machine of the modern kind; Nottingham became the centre of hosiery.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of frame-knit hosiery

materials.name: Jersey
materials.summary: A plain weft knit from the island knitters; Gabrielle Chanel made wool jersey into women's dress in 1916.

materials.name: Knitted wool
materials.photo: a folded swatch of knitted wool

materials.name: Brocade
materials.summary: A figured cloth with extra weft, often of metal thread, that floats on the face as a raised pattern; the cloth of court dress.

materials.name: Damask
materials.summary: A reversible figured cloth in which the pattern shows in satin on a ground of the opposite face; named after Damascus.

materials.name: Jacquard figured cloth
materials.summary: Cloth from a loom that lifts each warp thread by a punched card; the cards made large figured patterns cheap.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of jacquard figured cloth

materials.name: Velvet
materials.summary: A warp-pile cloth with a short dense pile cut from a second warp; Italian cities wove it for courts and the church.

materials.name: Chiffon
materials.summary: A sheer, floating plain weave of highly twisted yarn for overlays, scarves and evening dress.

materials.name: Crêpe de Chine
materials.summary: A light silk with a pebbled surface from crepe-twisted weft; it drapes well on the bias.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of crêpe de chine

materials.name: Taffeta
materials.summary: A crisp plain silk that rustles and holds a full skirt; the name comes from Persian 'taftah', twisted.

materials.name: Satin
materials.summary: A weave with long floats that gives a smooth, lustrous face; the name may come from Zaitun, the port of export.

materials.name: Flannel
materials.summary: A soft cloth that is napped after the weave; grey wool flannel became the suit and trouser cloth of the 20th century.

materials.name: Gabardine
materials.summary: A steep, tight twill of yarn proofed before the weave; it keeps out rain and lets the body breathe. The cloth of the trench coat.

materials.name: Harris Tweed
materials.summary: Hand-woven at home in the Outer Hebrides; the Orb mark dates from 1909 and an Act of Parliament protects the name since 1993.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of harris tweed

materials.name: Herringbone wool
materials.photo: a folded swatch of herringbone wool

materials.name: Houndstooth
materials.summary: A broken check from a 2/2 twill with four dark and four light yarns in warp and weft.

materials.name: Serge
materials.summary: A balanced twill with a clear diagonal rib, for uniforms, suits and coats.

materials.name: Silk twill
materials.summary: A fine, dense silk twill that takes a sharp print; it is the cloth of the printed square scarf and the necktie. Twill silk is in Chinese graves of the second century BC.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of silk twill

materials.name: Tartan
materials.summary: A twill check of coloured stripes in warp and weft; a check fragment from near Falkirk dates from about AD 250. The Dress Act of 1746 banned it in the Highlands.

materials.name: Tweed
materials.summary: A rough, thick twill of woollen yarn; the name comes from 'tweel', misread by a London merchant as the River Tweed.

materials.name: Worsted suiting
materials.summary: A smooth, firm cloth of combed long-staple yarn, named after the Norfolk village; the cloth of the tailored suit.
materials.photo: a folded swatch of worsted suiting
